newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to pursue large-scale privatisation - PM.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to pursue large-scale privatisation - PM.

text.p: Ukraine plans to draw up sales of shares in all large-scale enterprises by the first half of this year, Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said on Monday.

"By the first half of 1997 we will confirm the plan of placement of shares in all enterprises," he told a meeting of European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) directors, which arrived in Kiev for week-long meetings.
"We must end privatisation by the end of the year. We do not have time. We have to move ahead on large-scale privatisation by the first half of 1997," Lazarenko said.

The prime minister said the government also planned to issue shares in 105 of 228 companies which it has made available for strategic foreign investment, and would this week discuss whether to add another 40 enterprises to the list.
He said the president would pass a decree allowing the State Property Fund, the state privatisation agency, to privatise through foreign investment.
This would effectively overturn a parliamentary ruling late last year to stop privatisation through strategic foreign investment until the government developed rules to govern the process.
Although Ukraine has completed small-scale privatisation it has been criticised by international funding bodies for the overall slow pace of its privatisation programme.

It has started privatising only half of its 17,000 medium- and large-scale enterprises, and about 3,500 remain under a privatisation moratorium placed by parliament because they are considered "strategic" to national security.
